I had been wearing glasses for 12 years  and always knew I wanted to get rid of them permanently. Now, at 23 years old I finally decided to take that step. With a prescription of -7.5 and -7.75, I consulted Dr. S.K. Bulchandani about LASIK. He explained that ICL would be a better option for me because it doesn’t alter the cornea, offers better night vision, and has a lower risk of dry eyes. It sounded like the perfect solution for my needs.

Naturally, I was very nervous before the surgery. On the day of my first procedure (left eye), the anesthesiologist noticed how anxious I was and kindly reassured me. When I asked if someone could hold my hand during the procedure, she happily agreed, which immediately made me feel more comfortable.

The surgery itself was completely painless and surprisingly relaxing. The operating room had calming music and spiritual chants playing, creating a very peaceful atmosphere. The next day, when the patch from my left eye was removed, I was amazed to have 6/6 vision. Seeing clearly without glasses felt unreal.

I was much calmer for my right eye surgery, which went just as smoothly. While waiting after the procedure, I found myself reading the tiniest words on a poster across the room something I could never have imagined doing without glasses. Once the patch was removed, my right eye also achieved 6/6 vision.

The only side effect I noticed was seeing halos around bright lights, which is common after ICL surgery. However, now that I am 15 days post-surgery, they have reduced significantly and are only noticeable in certain lighting conditions.

I am extremely happy with my decision to undergo ICL surgery and grateful to Dr. S.K. Bulchandani and Trivision for their professionalism, expertise, and exceptional care throughout the entire journey.

featured_reviews.name: ritika ahuja
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dr. Hemant for blurred vision and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience.

Upon arrival, the assistant conducted a standard vision test and informed me that my vision was perfect as I was able to read even the smallest letters. A pressure test was also performed, and I was told that the results were normal.

After this, I was repeatedly asked whether anyone in my family had glaucoma. I clearly stated that no one in my family has a history of glaucoma. Despite being told that my initial tests appeared normal, I was advised to undergo additional tests costing approximately ₹2,400 each. After those tests, I was again informed that the reports looked normal, yet I was asked to undergo two more tests costing another ₹2,400 each because the doctor "wanted more clarity." At this stage, my bill had already reached around ₹11,600.

I requested to meet the doctor before proceeding further and was eventually allowed to do so. During the consultation, I felt that my concerns regarding blurred vision were not adequately addressed. When I repeatedly asked what was causing my symptoms, I was mostly told that I was anxious and overthinking. I was reassured that I would not go blind, but I did not receive a clear explanation of my diagnosis.

What confused me further was that I was prescribed Thyronorm 25 mcg despite informing the doctor that I do not have a thyroid condition. My thyroid reports were normal, yet I was advised to take the medication for two days without a clear explanation of why it was necessary.

I was then told to return after two days for pupil dilation and further examination, along with an additional consultation charge. I questioned why this could not be done during the same visit, especially after already undergoing multiple expensive tests, but no satisfactory explanation was provided.

The post-consultation experience was equally frustrating. The prescription did not mention when to take the prescribed medication, and I was advised to WhatsApp the doctor for clarification. Despite following up multiple times, I did not receive a timely response. I also requested copies of my reports but was told that the printer was not working. However, I observed other documents being printed during my visit. More than five days later, I still had not received all my reports as promised.

Another concern was the pricing of the tests. After my visit, I checked with other centres and found that similar tests are often charged between ₹900 and ₹1,200. This left me questioning why I was charged significantly higher amounts without a clear explanation.

I fully understand that specialist consultations and advanced diagnostics can be expensive when medically justified. However, as a patient, I felt pressured into undergoing multiple tests before receiving a proper explanation of my condition. The lack of transparency, poor communication, difficulty obtaining reports, and inadequate follow-up made this a very disappointing experience.

I hope this feedback encourages greater transparency, clearer communication with patients, and better post-consultation support in the future.
